cat: Coursework: Mechanics of Fracture and Fatigue
title: Fatigue Crack Growth and Retardation in CCT Panels

body.caption: Crack growth: baseline vs Wheeler vs Willenborg (2024-T3)

body: This project models fatigue crack growth and retardation in a center cracked tension panel, since aircraft structures accumulate cracks under repeated loading but occasional overload cycles can slow that growth down. I wanted to model this retardation effect, compare the two standard models used to predict it, and see how loading pattern and material choice change a structures usable life.

I built the analysis in MATLAB, starting with a baseline crack growth model using the Boeing Modified Walker equation, then implemented the Wheeler and Willenborg retardation models, which represent the same physical effect through different mechanisms. I ran parametric studies on overload frequency, overload timing, and repeated the full analysis for a second aluminum alloy to compare against the first.

The two models disagreed sharply, Wheeler predicted a 31 percent life increase from retardation while Willenborg predicted 100 percent for the same loading, since Willenborg acts on the driving stress before it enters a power law growth equation. More frequent and earlier overloads both extended life further, as expected.

The clearest result came from the material comparison. The stronger alloy had 33 percent higher yield strength but 29 percent lower fracture toughness, and it failed before the first scheduled overload ever occurred, so retardation had no effect at all. Higher strength alone did not make it the better choice for a damage tolerant application.
